key_path: Zero-account option: `atlas local setup` (Docker) gives a local deployment + connection string with no signup

Cloud: `atlas setup` (or `atlas auth register`/`atlas auth login`) opens browser for signup/login (Google/GitHub or email; email verification), creates a free M0 cluster, DB user and IP access list, and loads sample data

Connection string returned; for Admin API: create a Service Account (OAuth client credentials) in the org, or let an admin create an MCP Configuration that returns client id/secret + https://mcp.mongodb.com
human_gates: org_owner must enable AI client access for remote MCP (on by default only for orgs created at signup)

agent_native_auth.cli_browser_or_device_login: yes: `atlas auth login` browser/one-time-code flow; `atlas setup` end-to-end
agent_native_auth.oauth_dcr_for_mcp: yes for user-delegated: AI clients authorize through Atlas App Connections (OAuth) from the client's marketplace; programmatic uses MCP OAuth client-credentials extension
agent_native_auth.provisioning_api_mints_keys: yes: Admin API service accounts + MCP Configuration API (creates paired ingress/egress service accounts)
agent_native_auth.scoped_keys: yes: Atlas roles per service account / MCP configuration, read-only default, IP access list
agent_native_auth.test_dev_instances: yes: free M0 cluster; local Atlas deployments via Docker
agent_native_auth.free_tier: yes: M0 free forever, no card
agent_native_auth.keyless_claimable_dev_mode: partial: `atlas local` needs no account but is not claimable to cloud

product_mcp_remote.auth: OAuth via Atlas App Connections (user-delegated) or OAuth client-credentials (MCP configuration service accounts); mongodb-atlas-mcp-remote npx shim for clients lacking client-credentials

mcp.local: npx mongodb-mcp-server (connection string or Atlas service account; read-only mode)
mcp.docs_mcp: docs are exposed in the MCP ('docs-in-mcp' option on docs pages)
mcp.one_click: MongoDB MCP Plugin in Claude/Cursor/Gemini marketplaces

docs_for_agents.llms_txt: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/llms.txt (with a 'How agents should use this file' section, per-product llms.txt, Atlas CLI split into 5 parts)
docs_for_agents.llms_full_txt: none at root (404); product-level split files

score_justification: `atlas setup` gives a cluster + creds in one command, local dev needs no account, and there are two clean MCP access models. The cloud path still needs email verification, and remote MCP has an org-admin toggle.
best_practice: Separate MCP access models: user-delegated OAuth vs admin-provisioned MCP Configurations with ingress/egress service accounts, so egress creds are never exposed to the agent
biggest_gap: Remote MCP access is off by default for existing orgs; several auth concepts to learn (App Connections, service accounts, MCP configs, DB users)
notes: `atlas deployments` deprecated since Atlas CLI 1.52.0 in favor of `atlas local` / `atlas clusters`; Remote MCP release notes page says 'TBD'.
